subject: fileInput: upload progress bar does not display

messages.author: 80ac11e65419558c
messages.subject: fileInput: upload progress bar does not display
parts:
Hi,

I noticed that the fileInput function works, but the upload progress bar no longer displays when I use a variable name containing a period, e.g. "data.file" instead of "file1". Here I've pasted the code from the example "09_upload", except with file1 changed to data.file. Not sure why this is the case, is it a bug or something to do with naming syntax for HTML/javascript (not sure what this part runs on!)?

#----------------------------------------------------------------------
# ui.R
#----------------------------------------------------------------------
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("CSV Viewer"),
  sidebarPanel(
    fileInput('data.file', 'Choose CSV File',
              accept=c('text/csv', 'text/comma-separated-values,text/plain')),
    tags$hr(),
    checkboxInput('header', 'Header', TRUE),
    radioButtons('sep', 'Separator',
                 c(Comma=',',
                   Semicolon=';',
                   Tab='\t'),
                 'Comma'),
    radioButtons('quote', 'Quote',
                 c(None='',
                   'Double Quote'='"',
                   'Single Quote'="'"),
                 'Double Quote')
  ),
  mainPanel(
    tableOutput('contents')
  )
))
#----------------------------------------------------------------------
# server.R
#----------------------------------------------------------------------
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$contents <- renderTable({
    
    inFile <- input$data.file
    
    if (is.null(inFile))
      return(NULL)
    
    read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=input$header, sep=input$sep, quote=input$quote)
  })
})

messages.subject: Re: fileInput: upload progress bar does not display
parts:
TL;DR; For now avoid dots in input/output names as jQuery doesn't like it.

jQuery is the ubiqutious Javascript. It is used by Shiny to find elements in the webpage. 

To see an example of what I mean just 
  • run the 09 example runExample("09_upload")  is Chrome, and 
  • press Ctrl + Shift + J to bring up the JavaScript console.
  •  Now type in $("#file1") then you should see the below
[
  1. <input id=​"file1" type=​"file" accept=​"text/​csv,text/​comma-separated-values,text/​plain" class=​"shiny-bound-input">​
]

This code means to find in the HTML an element where the id = "file1" (basically anything after the "#" is the id). A . (dot) inside $ means to look for something with class = "whatever came after the dot".

So I believe Shiny is trying to run some code like $("#data.file") in Javascript. If you type  $("#data.file") into JavaScript console it should just return null. That's because $ is looking for an HTML element looking like this <... id = "data" class = "file" .... >. 
 
I think the Shiny team just need to escape the . (dot) when they see a dot in the input/output component name as in this stackoverflow question

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/350292/how-do-i-get-jquery-to-select-elements-with-a-period-in-their-id

Now if you type in $("data\\.file") then you should see the correct element returned. Unfortunately I believe this is a bug in Shiny for now.
